title: Frame (decision library)
description: One recurring venture problem, as a shape, at library/packages/<function>/frames/<id>.frame.json. A frame is to Naive what a component is to a React component library. It holds the goal, the decisions hidden in the founder's sentence, the premises that sentence assumes and the moves to attack them, and what current information a lookup must supply. It never holds an answer: no instrument, vendor, term or market norm, because those go stale and can be wrong. packages/naive/src/engine/frames.mjs matches a frame to the founder's words, reads the props from the venture's records, has a model judge each premise yes, no or unknown, and proposes the frame's decisions with open options for the founder to decide.

functions.description: The venture functions the problem belongs to; the first is the package the frame lives in

triggers.description: Sentences a founder says when they have this problem, in a founder's words

goal.description: The end the decisions serve; {prop} placeholders are filled from the venture

claim.description: What the founder's sentence assumes, as a yes/no proposition about this venture

attack.description: The premise attack applied to it, one of packages/naive/src/engine/frames.mjs ATTACKS

reads.description: The props the judgment of this premise needs

premises.description: The chain the founder's sentence assumes, in order

attacks.description: The premise attacks the frame uses (the hooks of the library)

dichotomy.description: The trade the founder's sentence forces, asked as: is it false, a real trade-off, or a sequence?

reframe.description: The better question the frame leaves the founder with; {prop} placeholders are filled from the venture

composes.description: Smaller frames this one is built from

props.description: The venture facts the frame reads, never stores: phase, goal, runway, revenue, cap_table, jurisdiction, control_rights

look_for.description: What a lookup must find, described as a problem, never as a named answer

freshness.description: What current information the frame needs and how fresh it must be. The lookup itself is a kit's skill; the frame says only what to look for.

reasoning.description: What a model that fetches the frame must do, in order

options.description: Options that describe the problem's own parts, never a named answer; options from a lookup are added at run time with their date and source

emits.description: The decisions the frame proposes, each open for the founder to decide

facts.description: The props of a worked venture

expect.description: The premise verdicts and dichotomy a good judgment reaches for these facts

cases.description: Worked cases, to evaluate a model's judgments against
